## Extraction of consensus FASTA from ddRAD loci
According to the analysis in `2023-05-17b`, I choose `ipyrad`'s output
corresponding to a clustering threshold of 0.95. I first generate FASTA
files for every locus, with different alleles of the same individual as
different sequences. That is, I will start by distributing allelic
sequences found in `../2023-05-17b/crepi95_outfiles/crepi95.alleles`
in locus-specific FASTA files. 

```{bash}
ALLELES=../2023-05-17b/crepi95_outfiles/crepi95.alleles
if [ ! -e summary_alleles.txt ]; then
   echo -e "Locus\tLength\tNumSeqs\tNumVar\tNumInfor" > summary_alleles.txt
   if [ ! -d alleles ]; then mkdir alleles; fi
   gawk '(/^[^\/]/){
      SEQ[$1] = $2
      N++
      LEN = length($2)
   }(/^\//){
      split($0, A, /\|/)
      N1 = gsub(/*/, "*", A[1])
      N2 = gsub(/-/, "-", A[1])
      FASTAOUT = sprintf("alleles/loc%05i.fa", A[2])
      for (s in SEQ) print ">" s "\n" SEQ[s] >FASTAOUT
      print sprintf("loc%05i.fa", A[2]) "\t" LEN "\t" N "\t" N1 + N2 + 0 "\t" N1 >>"summary_alleles.txt"
      delete SEQ
      N = 0
   }' $ALLELES
fi
```

```{r}
suppressMessages(library(kableExtra))
Alleles <- read.table('summary_alleles.txt', header = TRUE)
NumInd <- as.data.frame(table(Alleles$NumSeqs / 2), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(NumInd) <- c('NumInd', 'NumLoci')
NumInd$NumInd <- as.integer(NumInd$NumInd)
NumInd <- NumInd[order(NumInd$NumInd, decreasing = TRUE),]
NumInd$CumSum <- cumsum(NumInd$NumLoci)
plot(NumInd$NumInd, NumInd$CumSum,
     xlim = c(max(NumInd$NumInd), min(NumInd$NumInd)), type = 'l', log = 'y',
     xlab = 'Minimum number of individuals',
     ylab = 'Accumulated number of loci',
     main = 'Number of loci with at least so many individuals')
kable(NumInd, row.names = FALSE,
      col.names = c('Number of individuals', 'Number of loci', 'Cumulative Sum')) %>% kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

I use the `cons` program from EMBOSS to get the consensus sequence from every
locus.

```{bash}
if [ ! -e consensus.fa ]; then
   if [ ! -d tmp ]; then mkdir tmp; fi
   for l in $(ls -1 alleles); do
      cons -sequence alleles/$l -outseq tmp/$l -name ${l:0:8} 2> /dev/null
   done
   cat tmp/*.fa > consensus.fa
   rm -r tmp
fi
```

The file `consensus.fa` contains all loci, irrespective of how few
samples have been sequenced there. It can be used as a reference to
map original reads in FASTQ files, in order to generate the BAM files
corresponding to these loci. Mapping failures would reduce the coverage,
with respect to what is observed in the `alleles` folder. But in general
I would expect the mapping to generate similar alignments, with the
advantage of sequence quality information, from which to estimate
genotype likelihoods.

## What's next
In order to use the alignments for an extended Bayesian skyline plot,
I need to be able to assign population labels to individuals. One
option is to stick to the lake. But we know there is some more structure.
If I want to determine the structure of genetic variation before assuming
populations, I need a decent common matrix of genotypes.

One good reason not to have a complete matrix of genotypes is that
many reads were wasted in `ipyrad` due to low-coverage. We had set
the `mindepth_majrule` to 4, which excludes from the analysis any
sample-specific cluster with less than 4 reads. This makes sense for
the purpose of knowing genotypes, but it's a waste of information in
the context of genotype likelihoods.

One possibility is to run `ipyrad` again with `mindepth_majrule` set to
1. But we would lose the base-quality information with which genotype
likelihoods can be estimated, and we would miss a lot of heterozygous
genotypes. It may be worth trying, for the methods to be more consistent.
But it would be as having in every locus a mixture of haploid and diploid
individuals, without knowing which homozygotes are the haploid ones.

The strategy of re-mapping the raw reads to all cluster consensus seems
more promissing. That way, we would get BAM files, suitable to work with
ANGSD.
